Stanley Druckenmiller's Duquesne Family Office added 45% more shares of Sea (SE:NYSE) in the third quarter, according to its 13F for the quarter ended Sept. 30, filed Nov. 16. Sea's stock is down 26% since then.

He had plenty of company. Big funds also bought Alibaba (BABA:NYSE), Coupang (CPNG:NYSE) and MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) in the quarter. Three of the four stocks are lower since then, and Sea, Alibaba and Coupang are each about half below their 52-week highs.

Druckenmiller wasn't the biggest buyer of Sea

Duquesne held 1.59 million Sea shares worth $155 million on Sept. 30. That made Sea its seventh-biggest position, at 3.7% of the $4.15 billion of US stocks its 13F holds.

Burry said that he expanded his Adobe holding at approximately $246.

The investor is moving to donate a significant portion of his appreciated Alphabet shares, which he has owned since the COVID period.

'The Big Short' investor Michael Burry said on Monday that he closed some put positions while adding to long holdings including Adobe, MercadoLibre, QXO and Lululemon, and moved to donate a portion of long-held Alphabet shares.

Adobe Purchase And Outlook

Burry said that he expanded his Adobe holding at approximately $246, without clarifying the number of shares purchased. ADBE stock gained 1% on Monday to close at $246 after dropping nearly 30% year-to-date.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

"I continue to believe Adobe will successfully adapt, as will several other large software names, to the changing AI environment," Burry said. He noted that free substitutes for tools such as Adobe's Photoshop have existed for decades, yet Adobe has still grown revenue by 10% or more in each of the past four years.

In his view, Adobe's advantage lies in its standardized file formats, large installed base, enterprise contracts, and information security rather than superior AI models. Burry identifies the main risks as the cost of using external AI models and the pace of new subscription growth, but he argues the current valuation more than compensates for those concerns.

Puts Are Getting Expensive, Says Burry

Burry also exited his Oracle (ORCL) puts and closed the last of his Caterpillar (CAT) puts amid ongoing downward volatility in both stocks. He continues to hold a large put position in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF, along with puts on the Nasdaq 100, Nvidia, MetLife, and Palantir.

He noted that his overall short-put exposure "continues to grow in size, so trimming made sense." He is now looking at using outright short positions instead of or in addition to puts, because "puts, with the higher volatility of late, are getting expensive."

Burry's Additional Long Purchases

Beyond Adobe, Burry added to MercadoLibre (MELI) at about $1,480, elevating it to one of his largest positions alongside Australian retailer Temple & Webster. He also bought more QXO common stock near $12 and increased his Lululemon holding at roughly $106.

Lululemon's next earnings report is not expected until the second week of December, leaving the stock under pressure from a continued lack of new information, he said.

title: Can MercadoLibre's GMV Growth Fuel Long-Term Earnings Gains?

Can MercadoLibre's GMV Growth Fuel Long-Term Earnings Gains?
Sumit Singh
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 9:07 AM CST 4 min read
MELI
AMZN
SE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI continues to build momentum in Latin America's e-commerce market, supported by higher purchase frequency, expanding customer engagement and improving logistics efficiency. In third-quarter 2026, gross merchandise volume (GMV) reached $22.8 billion, increasing 38% year over year on a reported basis and 33% on an FX-neutral basis, while items sold rose 36% to 867 million. Unique active buyers increased approximately 22.3% to 93.9 million, highlighting sustained marketplace adoption and deeper customer engagement.

Brazil remains a major growth driver, with FX-neutral GMV advancing 36% and items sold rising 45%. The company's lower free-shipping threshold continues to encourage more frequent purchases, with items per buyer increasing 16% year over year. Management also reported stronger retention among customer cohorts acquired after the threshold reduction. However, smaller baskets and more free shipments have reduced shipping revenue per shipment. As a result, net shipping margin as a percentage of GMV has declined approximately 200 basis points since first-quarter 2025.

Meanwhile, Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% year over year in local currency and 14% compared with first-quarter 2025, reflecting improving logistics efficiency. In September, free and slow shipments in the R$19-R$79 price range became variable contribution-positive for the first time. MercadoLibre is also expanding its logistics capabilities, having opened 13 Metro fulfillment centers over the past 12 months and more than doubled the number of sorters and robots across its network. Management expects higher shipment density, automation and better network utilization to drive further cost improvements.

Still, stronger GMV growth has yet to translate fully into operating profitability. Third-quarter operating income declined 6% year over year to $676 million, while the operating margin reached 6.3%, down 40 basis points sequentially. Net shipping costs created a 60-basis-point margin headwind, reflecting increased free shipping, higher energy expenses and additional fulfillment capacity. Increased affiliate marketing investments in Brazil also pressured margins. Nevertheless, net income rose 6% to $448 million, supported by a lower tax rate and reduced foreign-exchange losses.

Management expects improving logistics productivity and greater operating scale to gradually reduce shipping costs relative to business volumes. MercadoLibre's ability to sustain purchase frequency while lowering fulfillment costs remains central to translating marketplace growth into stronger long-term earnings.

title: How Has eBay's Growth Story Changed?

How Has eBay's Growth Story Changed?
Trefis Team

eBay (EBAY) stock trades at 25.6 times earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. Shareholders paying that premium need to know what they are buying, yet management's priorities have changed. On its fiscal Q4 2024 call in February 2025, management emphasized a significant investment to overhaul consumer selling in the U.K., its second-largest market. On its latest call, management's U.K. remarks centered on consumer-selling growth, returns, and shipping initiatives. So what does management talk up now?

eBay Now Talks Up Depop Over Its U.K. Overhaul

On its fiscal Q3 2026 call on October 28, 2026, management said it is managing eBay and Depop as a portfolio. eBay recently acquired Depop, a secondhand fashion marketplace. Management called U.S. consumer fashion selling an underpenetrated market where it is building with two established brands, Depop and eBay.

Management said Depop's growth builds on eBay's consumer-selling momentum, the same business whose overhaul it made the case for in the U.K. in early 2025. On the fiscal Q4 2024 call, it said it had made a significant investment in its second-largest market through an overhaul of consumer selling in the U.K. On the fiscal Q2 2025 call in July 2025, management said growth in U.K. GMV, the value of goods sold, was comfortably above its level before that investment. eBay has since launched improvements to consumer selling in France and Italy, including free selling, but the U.K. overhaul no longer gets the airtime it once did.

Depop Is Growing Far Faster Than eBay Abroad

Depop's U.S. GMV more than doubled from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026, management said. Its active buyers over twelve months reached 11 million, up from 9 million. Depop is now part of eBay's totals: GMV grew nearly 16% to $23.2 billion before currency moves. Depop added nearly 3 points of that growth, and eBay grew 13% without it.

The U.K. sits inside eBay's international business, and that business grew far more slowly. International GMV grew nearly 4% in fiscal Q3 2026, against 22% for the U.S., both on an organic basis. Organic growth leaves out Depop.

Is Depop's Rise Good News For eBay Holders?

For the U.K., the change looks reassuring rather than worrying. Management said consumer-selling GMV grew more than 20% worldwide in fiscal Q3 2026, with healthy double-digit growth in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia. Even with less airtime, the business the overhaul set out to fix is still growing.

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) is retaining most of its gains this year despite significant economic volatility and political change. Excitement about artificial intelligence (AI) and confidence in the economy are strong growth drivers, and the market has been rallying after a post-election drop.

But not every stock is enjoying a strong run this year. And while stocks that drop can scare investors, that's where you can often find the best opportunities. Dutch Bros (NYSE:BROS), MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI), and On Holding (NYSE:ONON) are all plunging this year, but they have fantastic long-term potential.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's why these three stocks could be great additions to your portfolio.

Image source: Dutch Bros.

1. Dutch Bros: Down 43%

Dutch Bros is a small coffee shop chain with big ambitions. It has created a unique model with exclusive customer beverages and a store portfolio that's mostly drive-thrus, and it has attracted a large customer base that keeps coming back for more.

Part of the company's success comes from its menu, which leans toward the sweet and cold, setting it apart from the classic coffee shop. People also love its friendly customer service and focus on speed.

Management has been at the forefront of beverage innovation, including being the first major chain to offer boba when it became popular two years ago and launching its own line of Myst healthy energy drinks.

Revenue increased 30% year over year in the third quarter, and same-shop sales were up 4.4%. Net income increased from $27.3 million to $37.2 million.

Dutch Bros has 1,273 locations as of the end of the third quarter, and management says it has visibility to reach its goal of 2,029 stores by 2029. That's nearly double today's count, which could lead to doubling revenue over the next four or so years from new stores alone.

The market, however, was disappointed by the lowered full-year guidance. Management is navigating inflation and higher costs, which are impacting the business from top to bottom.

However, the long-term outlook is very strong, and Dutch Bros should reward shareholders who hold for the long term.

2. MercadoLibre: Down 25%

MercadoLibre operates the largest e-commerce business in Latin America as well as a thriving financial platform, including what it expects to become the largest digital bank in Mexico.

Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock fell approximately 20% from October 5 to November 10, closing at $1,490.24 after reaching a new 52-week low on November 5.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue and financial income rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but operating margin declined to 6.3% as shipping, fulfillment, and marketing investments pressured profitability.

Sea Limited (SE) reported 41.3% revenue growth at Shopee in the third quarter, while Nu Holdings (NU) provides another perspective on Brazilian consumer credit conditions.

MercadoLibre appears potentially undervalued following the selloff, although stronger margins and continued market share gains will be important to a sustained recovery.

What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock declined approximately 20% from its October 5 closing price of $1,860.61 to $1,490.24 on November 10, after hitting a new 52-week low on November 5.

The decline reflects two concerns: political uncertainty in Brazil and weaker-than-expected profitability despite strong revenue growth.

Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff delivered another term for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defeated Flávio Bolsonaro after trailing him in the first round.

MercadoLibre shares fell approximately 8% on October 26 as investors reassessed Brazil's economic outlook, currency risks, and consumer spending conditions.

Brazil generated approximately $15.2 billion of MercadoLibre's $28.9 billion in 2025 revenue, making it the company's largest market.

However, the company's third-quarter earnings report created a more immediate concern.

According to MercadoLibre's third-quarter financial results, revenue and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, but reported earnings of $8.83 per share fell short of the $9.27 consensus estimate cited in the initial research brief.

Operating margin declined to 6.3% from approximately 9.8% a year earlier, reflecting higher shipping expenses, expanded fulfillment capacity, and increased marketing spending in Brazil.

In its third-quarter shareholder letter, management described the pressure on shipping margins as "the price of the habit we set out to build."

The strategy is producing results. Items sold in Brazil increased more than 40% year over year for the fifth consecutive quarter, while MercadoLibre gained market share across its three largest markets.

Its lower free-shipping threshold also encouraged smaller purchases, initially putting pressure on shipping economics.

By September, Brazilian orders valued between R$19 and R$79 that qualified for free or slower delivery became variable contribution-positive for the first time, suggesting higher order volumes are beginning to improve shipping economics.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% from Nov. 3 to Nov. 10, with most of the damage in a 12% drop on Nov. 5, the day after its report. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 expected.

That spending comes as Shopee, owned by Sea Limited (SE:NYSE), pushes harder in Brazil, which Sea said on Nov. 10 was again its fastest-growing market. And MercadoLibre's credit sets a bar for Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE), which is expected to report on Nov. 12.

The miss was a choice

Operating income fell 6.6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin against 9.8% a year earlier. The company paid for more free shipping, added fulfillment space ahead of the holidays and stepped up affiliate marketing in Brazil. CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn told analysts the company is spending because the opportunity in front of it is large. "We have accepted a lower margin to do that," he said.

But the shipping bill is starting to shrink: Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency. And in September, orders between R19andR79, which now ship free, paid their own variable costs for the first time.

Shopee is pushing just as hard. It launched four-hour delivery in greater São Paulo in August with more than 4,000 partner stores, and Sea said on Nov. 10 that the service now runs from more than 7,000. MercadoLibre began testing one-hour delivery in parts of the city in September. Sea also said Shopee again grew faster than Brazil's broader market in the third quarter.
